findings.passage: House Bill 2005 was passed by the majority party earlier this week. This will strip the following rights from Oregonians:
findings.note: Her official e-newsletter, criticising HB 2005 B. It lists: criminalising owners by the type of gun, possession limits for adults aged 18 to 20, and differing gun laws across jurisdictions.
subjects: minimum age to own a gun

findings.passage: The U.S. Supreme Court has previously ruled that laws like this are unconstitutional. Immediately after the passage of HB 2005, the House Republicans committed to donating $25,000 to support impending litigation to protect the Second Amendment rights of Oregonians.
findings.note: Her official e-newsletter says HB 2005 is unconstitutional and reports the House caucus pledge of money for a court challenge.

findings.passage: “House Bill 3076 was a clear violation of Oregonians’ constitutional rights,” said Representative Lucetta Elmer (R-McMinnville). “It would have harmed local businesses and law-abiding gun owners alike. I am thrilled that it will no longer be moving this session.”
findings.note: Quote of her in a House caucus release on sending HB 3076B (state licensing of firearm dealers) back to committee.

findings.passage: The bill infringes on Oregonians’ Second Amendment rights by turning those who already own bump stocks and other attachments into criminals, replaces public safety with a door sign, and creates confusion across jurisdictions for concealed handgun license carriers.
findings.note: Her official e-newsletter on SB 243C (bump stocks, signage in place of carry, carry licence rules, delay of Measure 114). The same item reports caucus amendments she does not name herself as moving: repeal Measure 114, carry reciprocity, legalise suppressors; all rejected.
